title: Turn an enclosed wall footprint into a room with a tag and a reported area
task: Create a Room in an enclosed footprint with Document.Create.NewRoom(level, UV), tag it with NewRoomTag(new LinkElementId(room.Id), UV, viewId) in the level's floor plan, and read Room.Area. On a level the script created, set LEVEL_ROOM_COMPUTATION_HEIGHT first or the room may report zero area; NewRoomTag takes a LinkElementId, not an ElementId.

pitfalls.symptom: Room.Area is 0 and GetBoundarySegments is empty although walls enclose the point (issue #118).
pitfalls.cause: On a script-created level the room computation height can sit outside the walls' extent.
pitfalls.fix: Set the level's LEVEL_ROOM_COMPUTATION_HEIGHT (e.g. 4.0 feet) before placing the room (step 1).

pitfalls.symptom: NewRoomTag does not accept the room's ElementId.
pitfalls.cause: Its first parameter is a LinkElementId, because the room may be in a linked model.

pitfalls.symptom: NewRoomTag throws an ArgumentNullException deep inside Revit.
pitfalls.cause: No plan view is scoped to the room's level (Level.Create makes none).
pitfalls.fix: Create the plan with ViewPlan.Create and tag in it.

pitfalls.cause: Room has no native class to filter on.
